questions.question: Day 7 Practice (Performance Reviews & Goals): When talking about withdrawing cash from ATM (yesterday afternoon), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'Our neighbor'?

options.d: I am withdrawing cash from ATM right now.

questions.explanation:

Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "Is this card accepted at the cash withdrawal counter?".

questions.question: Day 7 Vocabulary (Performance Reviews & Goals): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'fill out'?

options.a: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.b: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.c: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.d: Complete an official form.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
'fill out' means: complete an official form. Example: "Please fill out this registration form."

questions.question:
Day 7 Translation Scenario 1 (Performance Reviews & Goals):

Telugu: "ముందుగా సమస్య యొక్క మూలకారణాన్ని కనుగొనాలి."
(Literal attempt: "First problem root cause finding wanted.")

options.a: First and foremost, we must identify the root cause of the issue.
options.b: I am needing to first problem root cause finding wanted.
options.c: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.d: First problem root cause finding wanted.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
Natural Version: "First and foremost, we must identify the root cause of the issue."

Use 'First and foremost' and 'identify the root cause'.

questions.question:
Day 7 Translation Scenario 2 (Performance Reviews & Goals):

Telugu: "రేపటి మీటింగ్ 3 గంటలకు రీషెడ్యూల్ చేయవచ్చా?"
(Literal attempt: "Tomorrow meeting 3 clock reschedule possible?")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: Tomorrow meeting 3 clock reschedule possible?
options.c: Could we reschedule tomorrow's meeting to 3:00 PM?
options.d: I am needing to tomorrow meeting 3 clock reschedule possible?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option C
Natural Version: "Could we reschedule tomorrow's meeting to 3:00 PM?"

Use 'Could we reschedule...' for polite professional requests.

questions.question:
Day 7 Translation Scenario 3 (Performance Reviews & Goals):

questions.question:
Day 7 Translation Scenario 4 (Performance Reviews & Goals):

Telugu: "అన్నా, బస్టాండ్ దగ్గర డ్రాప్ చేయండి, ఎంత అవుతుంది?"
(Literal attempt: "Brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: Brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?
options.c: Please drop me off near the bus stand. How much is the fare?
options.d: I am needing to brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?
